thread:
akash: Hey team — quick heads up: I’m on OPT STEM (EAD expires May 15). Currently in India getting the consular stamp for an H-1 transfer. Offer start is booked for May 20. Two asks: 1) can benefits be activated if my I-9 and visa stamping are still pending? 2) payroll / first paycheck timing if start is delayed by consulate delays?

tess (recruiter): @akash thanks for flagging. We can be flexible on start — do you have an ETA for your stamping appointment? Also send your passport + I-797 once you have it.

akash: Appointment is May 10 but consulate processing might push to late May. Worst case could be 2–3 weeks delay. I’d prefer to keep May 20 if possible (remote onboarding).

maria (People Ops): Short version: benefits kick in after your I-9 is completed and you’re on payroll. We can’t enroll someone who isn’t legally authorized to work at the point payroll starts. So if the I-9 can’t be completed by day 1, we need to either delay benefits effective date or delay your payroll start.

jordan (Payroll): To add: payroll cutoff is the 25th for the first of the next month, so if you start May 20 and your I-9 isn’t done by then, we can’t process payroll retroactively without completed authorization docs. If you end up starting after May 31, you’d show on the June payroll.

akash: Ok — any interim alternatives? unpaid start? contractor? I prefer to avoid gaps in benefits if possible.

maria (People Ops): We can’t make someone an employee on payroll without work authorization. Options we’ve used historically: 1) delay official start date until after stamping/I-9 — preserves benefits enrollment timing; 2) start onboarding (non-pay, no benefits) — e.g., internal training access but no payroll; 3) in exceptional cases, contractors have been engaged but that requires a separate SOW and approvals (slow). Which would you prefer?

akash: Probably option 2 (onboarding-only) so I can start ramping. I just need access to docs/Slack. Will that block stock / offer acceptance paperwork?

maria (People Ops): You can accept the offer and sign equity docs now. Stock grant vesting will use your official hire date (we can set that to your payroll start). For equity paperwork we can proceed. For benefits: we’ll set the benefits effective date to the date your I-9 completes and payroll starts.

tess (recruiter): Action items: @akash share passport + appointment confirmation, @maria to send a travel letter template for consulate, @jordan to note payroll implications.

jordan (Payroll): I’ll add a note to payroll: if docs come in before the payroll cutoff we can try to include you in May; otherwise June. Also advise on temporary access provisioning (IT) billing.

maria (People Ops): Travel letter template (sample below) — take this to the consulate. Please customize and we’ll sign.

```
To: Consular Officer
Subject: Employment verification / travel support for visa stamping
Employee: Akash Rao
Role: Software Engineer (Full-time)
Start date (proposed): May 20, 2026
Company: Redwood Inference, Inc.
We verify that the above named individual has a bona fide job offer and supporting documentation will be provided upon request. Please contact hr@redwood.com for verification.
```

akash: That helps, thank you. One more Q — for I-9 remote verification, can Redwood use an authorized representative in-country to review originals?

maria (People Ops): Yes — we can use the authorized representative option. You’ll need to present originals to the rep on your first physical day of work in the US. For now we’ll use remote I-9 attestation to capture scanned docs, but originals must be inspected later. I’ll DM the checklist.

hr-bot: Reminder: new hire packet (tax, direct deposit, benefits enrollment) auto-sent when payroll start date is set.

tess (recruiter): tagging this thread — @akash please upload appointment proof to the candidate portal and I’ll coordinate paperwork. If consulate slips, we’ll update hire date and confirm benefits window.

akash: Uploaded appointment email and passport scan. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

maria (People Ops): Got it. I’ll draft the signed travel letter once you confirm the consulate location. We’ll plan onboarding-only access on May 20 and hold payroll until I-9 is cleared unless you tell us otherwise.

jordan (Payroll): Noted — holding payroll unless I-9 clears. Reach out if you need a payroll exception; we’ll need legal signoff.

akash: Appreciate it. Will update after appointment.

maria (People Ops): Thanks — sending DM with checklist and the authorized rep form now.
